verdict: CVS Health's revenue rose 5.4% to $108.4B and profit bounced back to $2.2B, as its Aetna insurance business improved sharply and last year's $5.7B goodwill impairment did not repeat.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenues were $108.4B, vs $102.9B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $3.13 loss a year ago, when results included a $5.7B goodwill impairment; adjusted EPS was $2.09

kpis.label: Health Care Benefits adj. operating income
kpis.note: The Aetna insurance business — nearly triple the $314M of a year ago, as the medical benefit ratio improved to 91.3% from 92.8%

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: The company's own non-GAAP measure, vs $1.60 a year ago; full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to at least $8.20

segments.name: Pharmacy products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold through CVS pharmacies and its pharmacy-benefit business (the statement's 'Products' line) — by far the biggest revenue source. Up 7%, helped by drug mix and brand-price inflation.

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from Aetna members and employers. Up 3%, as growth in government business outweighed the exit from individual exchange plans.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for care itself — clinics, home health and other health services. Roughly flat vs a year ago.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Income from the investment portfolio held to back insurance obligations.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Running the stores, clinics and insurance operations — staff, rent, technology and admin. It includes a $193M Omnicare guarantee charge and $425M of amortization of acquired intangibles that the company leaves out of its adjusted figures.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. The health care costs in cost of revenue are $32,316M (members' medical care) and the cost of products sold is $61,185M (mainly drugs bought for resale). The flow uses consolidated net income of $2,171M; net income attributable to CVS Health was $2,172M, as noncontrolling interests absorbed a $1M loss.

takeaways.title: Growth in every business
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5.4% to $108.4B. Health Services — the pharmacy-benefit business that negotiates drug prices for employers and health plans — grew fastest, up 9.5% to $54.0B on drug mix and brand inflation, while store revenue dipped 2.0% on drug-price cuts and reimbursement pressure, partly offset by the Rite Aid stores and prescription files CVS bought in 2025.

takeaways.title: Aetna's recovery carried profit
takeaways.text: The medical benefit ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — improved to 91.3% from 92.8% a year ago. Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income nearly tripled to $912M from $314M, and company-wide adjusted operating income rose 21% to $4.2B.

takeaways.title: Back in profit — and guidance raised
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $1.68, vs a $3.13 loss a year ago that included a $5.7B goodwill impairment (writing down the value of a past acquisition). Adjusted EPS was $2.09 vs $1.60. CVS raised full-year 2026 guidance — adjusted EPS to at least $8.20 and operating cash flow to at least $15.5B.

oneTimers: Operating expenses include a $193M charge for an estimated guarantee liability tied to Omnicare, the long-term-care pharmacy business CVS separated from in September 2025. CVS excludes it from adjusted earnings.

The gap between GAAP operating income ($3,566M) and adjusted operating income ($4,194M) also reflects $425M of amortization of intangible assets from past acquisitions and $13M of acquisition-integration costs, partly offset by a $3M net realized capital gain.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $747M on CVS's debt, partly offset by $30M of other income, for a net $717M cost below operating income.
footerNote: Flow adaptation: CVS reports no gross-profit line; cost of revenue combines health care costs and the cost of products sold.
